summary: Repaired node1’s document reader. It now completes 500 reads with a soft file-descriptor limit of 64, consistently returns length 42, cleans up resources on failure paths, preserves the count argument and document, and survives reboot.
actions_performed: Removed the retained file-handle list and used a context manager per read.
Updated the shebang to the installed `/usr/bin/python3` interpreter.
Verified cleanup after injected read and open failures.
Rebooted node1 once and verified recovery and persistence.

evidence.requirement: Process at least 500 successive reads under soft open-file limit 64 with identical lengths
evidence.summary: Before repair, descriptor exhaustion occurred after 61 reads. After repair, all 500 reads completed successfully and returned length 42.
An injected read failure closed the acquired file; 500 injected open failures left the descriptor count unchanged at 4.

evidence.requirement: Retain count argument and keep supplied document unchanged
evidence.summary: The count argument produced exactly 500 outputs. document.txt retained size 42, inode 262327, original timestamp, mode, and checksum through reboot.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged before and after restart.

Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45 to e7620448-1f03-4dfa-8bea-b3a1a4f8e6c3; checksums and the 500-read constrained test remained healthy afterward.
